metadata.catalogName: Lunar Exploration Candidate & Benchmark Landing Sites
metadata.lineage: NASA Artemis 2024 candidate regions, CLPS mission flight manifests, and Apollo/CNSA ground truth baselines
metadata.officialUpdateNotice: Includes 9 official Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024 update), polar benchmarks, CLPS landers (IM-1, IM-2, Blue Ghost), and historic reference sites (Apollo 11, Apollo 17, Chang'e 6).
metadata.coordinateConvention: IAU/IAG Lunar Mean Earth / Polar Axis (ME)
metadata.elevationDatum: Reference lunar sphere of R = 1737.4 km (LOLA DEM 128ppd)

sites.name: Shackleton Crater Rim
sites.description: Prominent elevated rim point located less than 3 km from the exact South Pole. Features near-constant solar grazing illumination during southern summer and excellent Earth visibility.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis 2022 Study Shortlist / LOLA Topography
sites.missionContextNote: Topographic ridge feature near Shackleton rim investigated for Artemis surface operations.

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.description: Structural ridge connecting Shackleton to de Gerlache rim. Highly rated for solar power generation potential, with periodic low-angle shadowing by adjacent massifs.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis 2022 Study Shortlist / LOLA Topography
sites.missionContextNote: High illumination ridge featured in 2022 preliminary candidate evaluations.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 1
sites.description: Western rim crest of de Gerlache crater overlooking steep permanently shadowed interior depressions while maintaining periodic line-of-sight to Earth.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis 2022 Study Shortlist / LOLA Topography
sites.missionContextNote: Adjacent to updated de Gerlache Rim 2 candidate region announced in Oct 2024.

sites.name: Peak Near Shackleton
sites.description: Distinctive topographic high point east of Shackleton crater rim. Receives elongated periods of low-elevation solar illumination.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis 2022 Study Shortlist / LOLA Topography
sites.missionContextNote: Topographic elevation point for extreme polar illumination studies.

sites.name: Amundsen Crater Rim
sites.description: Standard benchmark site utilized for cross-calibrating solar illumination models against LROC Narrow Angle Camera shadow sequences.
sites.sourceCatalog: LROC NAC Calibration Benchmark Series
sites.missionContextNote: Reference site used for shadow-length ground truthing against empirical camera passes.

sites.name: Malapert Mountain (Massif)
sites.description: Major topographic massif rising ~5 km above surroundings. Outstanding direct-to-Earth communication line of sight and wide geometric horizon clearance.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis 2022 / Oct 2024 Candidate Region List
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.missionContextNote: One of the nine official Artemis III candidate regions re-confirmed in October 2024.

sites.name: Haworth Crater Rim
sites.description: Elevated rim of Haworth crater, which shelters deep permanently shadowed regions (PSRs) with volatile deposits. Complex local horizon profile.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis 2022 / Oct 2024 Candidate Region List
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.missionContextNote: One of the nine official Artemis III candidate regions re-confirmed in October 2024.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1
sites.description: High-latitude crater rim area targeted by volatile investigation rovers. Balanced mix of accessible slopes, illumination windows, and Earth line-of-sight.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis 2022 / Oct 2024 Candidate Region List
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.missionContextNote: Confirmed Artemis III candidate landing region and VIPER exploration zone.

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.description: Highest topographic summit in the lunar south polar region (~6.1 km above datum), named in honor of NASA mathematician Melba Roy Mouton. Extraordinary line-of-sight across the entire polar basin.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis III October 2024 Candidate Region Announcement
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.missionContextNote: Official Artemis III candidate landing region named after Melba Roy Mouton.

sites.name: Mons Mouton Plateau
sites.description: Expansive elevated plateau adjacent to Mons Mouton summit. Offers exceptional surface traversability, stable slopes, and uninterrupted Earth visibility windows.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis III October 2024 Candidate Region Announcement
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.officialRegionReference: Mons Mouton Plateau (NASA Oct 2024 Confirmed Region)
sites.missionContextNote: Primary high-elevation landing candidate featuring benign surface landing slopes.

sites.name: Slater Plain
sites.description: High-latitude polar plain named in honor of planetary scientist Elizabeth Slater. Benign planar relief providing high landing security with access to Faustini rim ejecta.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis III October 2024 Candidate Region Announcement
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.missionContextNote: Benign inter-crater plain candidate selected for rover mobility and descent safety.

sites.name: Peak near Cabeus B
sites.description: Prominent ridge point overlooking Cabeus crater, the site of LCROSS volatile water confirmation. Exceptional scientific proximity to volatile cold-traps.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis III October 2024 Candidate Region Announcement
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.officialRegionReference: Peak near Cabeus B (NASA Oct 2024 Confirmed Region)
sites.missionContextNote: Overlooks Cabeus volatile-rich crater floor where LCROSS detected hydroxyl/water ice.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 2
sites.description: Secondary ridge section along Nobile crater rim. Features extended thermal stability and strategic access to VIPER-mapped volatile deposits.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis III October 2024 Candidate Region Announcement
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.missionContextNote: Southern crater rim high point designated in refined Artemis III candidate set.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 2
sites.description: Eastern summit ridge of de Gerlache crater providing elongated summer illumination and direct visual corridor to Shackleton connecting ridges.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Artemis III October 2024 Candidate Region Announcement
sites.catalogVersion: Confirmed in Oct 2024 Artemis III 9-Region Update
sites.officialRegionReference: de Gerlache Rim 2 (NASA Oct 2024 Confirmed Region)
sites.missionContextNote: Updated de Gerlache candidate region confirmed in NASA October 2024 release.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A)
sites.description: Intuitive Machines IM-1 Nova-C lander "Odysseus". First commercial US lunar landing (Feb 22, 2024), situated near Malapert A crater at 80°S.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS)
sites.missionContextNote: Ground truth commercial polar benchmark with confirmed radio transmission metrics.

sites.name: IM-2 PRIME-1 (Connecting Ridge)
sites.description: NASA CLPS volatile extraction payload lander featuring TRIDENT drill and MSolo mass spectrometer for sub-surface regolith ice mining on Shackleton ridge.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS)
sites.officialRegionReference: Shackleton Connecting Ridge Ice Drill Target
sites.missionContextNote: First dedicated polar drill site designed to assess volatiles at 1-meter depth.

sites.name: Firefly Blue Ghost 1 (Mare Crisium)
sites.description: NASA CLPS payload delivery mission to the basaltic floor of Mare Crisium basin. Investigates regolith properties, heat flow, and solar wind interactions.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS)
sites.missionContextNote: Near-equatorial mare reference demonstrating classical 14-day day/night diurnal cycle.

sites.name: Apollo 11 Tranquility Base
sites.description: First crewed lunar landing site (July 20, 1969). Standard equatorial reference baseline: Sun reaches high zenith (>89°), Earth sits overhead at ~60°, and illumination cycles predictably across 14d light / 14d dark.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Apollo Lunar Landing Sites Registry
sites.missionContextNote: Canonical equatorial planetary baseline showing why South Pole polar navigation is unique.

sites.name: Apollo 17 Taurus-Littrow
sites.description: Final Apollo crewed mission (Dec 1972) situated in a narrow lunar graben valley flanked by 2-km high North and South Massifs. Illustrates dramatic valley-wall horizon blockage.
sites.sourceCatalog: NASA Apollo Lunar Landing Sites Registry
sites.missionContextNote: Standard planetary baseline for massive terrain horizon masking in a lunar valley.

sites.name: Chang'e 6 Apollo Basin (Far Side)
sites.description: First far-side sample return landing site (June 2024, South Pole-Aitken Apollo basin). Serves as critical baseline proving 0% direct-to-Earth communication (Earth permanently sub-horizon, requiring Queqiao relay).
sites.sourceCatalog: CNSA Lunar Exploration Program / International PDS
sites.missionContextNote: Benchmark for complete Earth communication blackout without orbital relay support.
